I've been doing this for 35 years on the North China Plain. My father farmed this land before me. Wheat in winter, maize in summer — that's the only system that makes sense here in Quzhou. The whole 5 mu rotates together.

**My thinking:**

For wheat, I'll plant in early October like always. I'll use an improved variety — Jimai 22 or Kenong 199, whatever the seed shop in town has. I stopped using traditional seed a long time ago because yields just aren't worth it. I do three irrigations on wheat: once before the ground freezes in November, once at jointing in late March, once at heading in May. My well can handle it. I apply fertilizer in two splits — base at planting, urea topdress at jointing. For pests I spray twice, once for aphids in spring, once for powdery mildew if I see it coming. I use rotary tillage after maize harvest to break up the straw — my little walking tractor handles that fine.

For summer maize, I go straight into the field after wheat harvest in June. No time to waste — every day counts in the summer growing window. I direct-seed with no-till. I use hybrid seed, always Zhengdan 958 or Xianyu 335, nothing else in this area makes sense. I put down compound fertilizer at planting and top up with urea around knee-height. Summer rains usually help but I keep my pump ready. Two irrigations planned — one at emergence if it's dry, one at silking. One pesticide application for corn borer.

My kids work in the city. I manage this mostly myself plus my wife during busy periods. I keep inputs moderate — I can't afford to overdo it and the land doesn't need it.
